verses.14:24: the one who does not love Me does not keep My words. And the word that you have heard is not Mine, but His who sent Me, the Father.
verses.14:25: These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you.
verses.14:26: But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, He will teach you all things and remind you of everything that I have said to you.
verses.14:27: Peace I leave to you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you in the way the world gives. Do not let your heart be troubled, nor be frightened.
verses.14:28: You have heard that I said to you, 'I am going away, and I am coming to you.' If you loved Me, you would certainly rejoice because I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I.
verses.14:29: And now I have told you before it takes place, so that when it has taken place, you may believe.
verses.14:30: I will no longer speak many things with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in Me.
verses.14:31: But so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father gave Me a commandment, so I do. Rise, let us go from here."
verses.15:1: "I am the true vine, and My Father is the farmer.
verses.15:2: Every branch in Me not bearing fruit, He will take it away, and every one that bears fruit, He will prune it, so that it may yield more fruit.
verses.15:3: You are clean already on account of the word that I have spoken to you.
verses.15:4: Remain in Me, and I in you. Just as a branch cannot bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in Me.
verses.15:5: I am the vine; you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, he bears much fruit, because without Me you can do nothing.
verses.15:6: If anyone does not remain in Me, he will be thrown out like a branch and will wither; and they will gather him and throw him into the fire, and he burns.
verses.15:7: If you remain in Me, and My words remain in you, you will ask for whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
verses.15:8: In this My Father has been glorified, that you yield very much fruit and become My disciples.
verses.15:9: Just as the Father loved Me, I also loved you. Remain in My love.
verses.15:10: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I also have kept My Father's commandments and remain in His love.
verses.15:11: These things I have spoken to you, so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be made full.
verses.15:12: This is My commandment: that you love each other as I loved you.
verses.15:13: No one has greater love than this: that a person lay down his life for his friends.
verses.15:14: You are My friends if you do the things that I command you.
verses.15:15: I will no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because all things that I have heard from My Father I have made known to you.
verses.15:16: You did not choose Me; rather, I chose you and appointed you so that you may go and yield fruit, and your fruit may remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He may give to you.
verses.15:17: I command you these things: that you love each other.
verses.15:18: If the world hates you, know that it hated Me before you.
verses.15:19: If you had been of the world, the world would love what was its own; yet because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
verses.15:20: Remember My word that I told you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
verses.15:21: But they will do all these things to you on account of My name, because they do not know Him who sent Me.
verses.15:22: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; yet now they have no excuse for their sin.
verses.15:23: Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
verses.15:24: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would have no sin; yet now they have both seen and hated both Me and My Father.
verses.15:25: But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: 'They hated Me without cause.'
verses.15:26: But when the Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, He will bear witness about Me;
verses.15:27: and you will bear witness, because you have been with Me from the beginning."
verses.16:1: "These things I have spoken to you so that you may not be made to stumble.
verses.16:2: They will exclude you from the synagogues; but an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will suppose that he is rendering service to God.
verses.16:3: And they will do these things to you, because they have not known the Father, nor Me.
verses.16:4: But these things I have spoken to you so that when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you.
verses.16:5: Yet I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you. And now I am going to Him who sent Me, and none of you questions Me, 'Where are You going?'
verses.16:6: But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
verses.16:7: Yet I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go; for if I do not depart, the Paraclete will not come to you, but if I depart, I will send Him to you.
verses.16:8: And when He comes, He will convict the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment.
verses.16:9: Concerning sin, because they have not believed in Me.
verses.16:10: Concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father, and you will no longer see Me.
verses.16:11: And concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has already been judged.
verses.16:12: I still have many things to tell you, yet you cannot bear them at present.
verses.16:13: But when He, the Spirit of truth, comes, He will teach you all truth; for He will not speak from Himself, but whatever He hears He will speak, and He will declare to you the things that are to come.
verses.16:14: He will glorify Me, because He will receive from what is Mine and declare it to you.
verses.16:15: All things that the Father has are Mine. For this reason I said that He will receive from what is Mine and declare it to you.
verses.16:16: A little while, and you will no longer see Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me, because I am going to the Father."
verses.16:17: Then some of His disciples said to each other, "What is this that He is saying to us, 'A little while, and you will not see Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me,' and, 'Because I am going to the Father'?"
verses.16:18: So they were saying, "What is this that He says, 'A little while'? We do not know what He is speaking about."
verses.16:19: Now Jesus knew that they wanted to question Him, and He said to them, "You are inquiring among yourselves about this, because I said, 'A little while, and you will not see Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me.'
verses.16:20: Amen, amen, I tell you, you will wail and weep, while the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, yet your sorrow will be turned into joy.
verses.16:21: When a woman is giving birth, she has sorrow, because her hour has come; but when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the distress on account of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
verses.16:22: Therefore you also have sorrow now; yet I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
verses.16:23: And on that day you will not ask Me anything. Amen, amen, I tell you, if you ask the Father for anything in My name, He will give it to you.
verses.16:24: Up to now you have not asked for anything in My name; ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.
verses.16:25: These things I have spoken to you in proverbs. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but will declare to you plainly concerning the Father.
verses.16:26: On that day you will ask in My name; and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf,
verses.16:27: for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came forth from God.
verses.16:28: I came forth from the Father and came into the world; again, I am leaving the world and going to the Father."
verses.16:29: His disciples say to Him, "Look, now You are speaking plainly and saying no proverb;
verses.16:30: now we know that You know all things and have no need for anyone to question You; by this we believe that You came forth from God."
verses.16:31: Jesus replied to them, "Do you believe now?
verses.16:32: Look, an hour is coming, and has already come, when you will be scattered, each one to his own home, and will leave Me alone; yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
verses.16:33: These things I have spoken to you so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have distress; but take courage, I have conquered the world."
verses.17:1: Jesus spoke these things, and raising His eyes to heaven, He said, "Father, the hour has come; glorify Your Son, so that Your Son may glorify You,
verses.17:2: just as You gave Him authority over all flesh, so that to all that You have given Him He may give eternal life.
verses.17:3: Now this is eternal life: that they may know You, the only true God, and Him whom You sent, Jesus Christ.
verses.17:4: I glorified You on the earth; I have completed the work that You gave Me to do.
verses.17:5: And now, You, Father, glorify Me with Yourself, with the glory that I had with You before the world was.
verses.17:6: I have manifested Your name to the people whom You gave Me out of the world. They were Yours, and You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
verses.17:7: Now they have come to know that all the things You have given Me are from You,
verses.17:8: because the words that You gave Me I have given to them, and they themselves received them, and truly came to know that I came forth from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
verses.17:9: I pray for them; I do not pray for the world, but for these whom You have given Me, because they are Yours,
verses.17:10: and everything of Mine is Yours, and what is Yours is Mine; and I have been glorified in them.
verses.17:11: And I am no longer in the world, and these are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, keep them in Your name, those whom You have given Me, so that they may be one, just as We also are.
verses.17:12: While I was with them, I was keeping them in Your name. Those whom You gave Me I have guarded, and not one of them perished except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture may be fulfilled.
verses.17:13: But now I am coming to You, and I speak these things in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within themselves.
verses.17:14: I have given them Your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I also am not of the world.
verses.17:15: I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from evil.
verses.17:16: They are not of the world, just as I also am not of the world.
verses.17:17: Sanctify them in truth. Your word is truth.
verses.17:18: Just as You sent Me into the world, I also sent them into the world;
verses.17:19: and on their behalf I sanctify Myself, so that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
verses.17:20: Now I do not pray for them alone, but also for those who will believe in Me through their word,
verses.17:21: that they all may be one, just as You, Father, are in Me and I in You, that they themselves also may be one in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
verses.17:22: And the glory that You gave Me I have given to them, so that they may be one, just as We also are one:
verses.17:23: I in them and You in Me, so that they may be made complete as one, and that the world may know that You sent Me and loved them, just as You also loved Me.
verses.17:24: Father, I desire that where I am, those whom You have given Me may also be with Me, so that they may see My glory, which You gave Me, because You loved Me before the founding of the world.
verses.17:25: Righteous Father, the world has not known You, yet I have known You, and these have come to know that You sent Me.
verses.17:26: And I have made Your name known to them, and will make it known, so that the love with which You have loved Me may be in them, and I in them."
verses.18:1: When Jesus had said these things, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron stream, where there was a garden, into which He Himself and His disciples entered.
verses.18:2: Now Judas also, who was betraying Him, knew the place, because Jesus had frequently met there with His disciples.
verses.18:3: Judas, therefore, having taken a cohort and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
verses.18:4: Jesus, therefore, knowing all things that were about to come upon Him, stepped forward and said to them, "Whom are you seeking?"
verses.18:5: They answered Him, "Jesus the Nazarene." Jesus said to them, "I am." Now Judas also, who was betraying Him, was standing with them.
verses.18:6: So when He said to them, "I am," they went backward and fell to the ground.
verses.18:7: Therefore He questioned them again, "Whom are you seeking?" And they said, "Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.18:8: Jesus answered, "I told you that I am. Therefore, if you are seeking Me, let these go away."
verses.18:9: This was so that the word He spoke might be fulfilled: "Of those whom You have given Me, I have not lost a single one."
verses.18:10: Simon Peter, therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant, and cut off his right ear. Now the servant's name was Malchus.
verses.18:11: Jesus therefore said to Peter, "Put your sword into the sheath. The cup that the Father has given Me, will I not drink it?"
verses.18:12: So the cohort, and the tribune, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound Him.
verses.18:13: And they led Him to Annas first, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was the high priest of that year.
verses.18:14: Now Caiaphas was the one who had given counsel to the Jews that it is expedient for one man to die for the people.
verses.18:15: Now Simon Peter was following Jesus, and so was another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, and he entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
verses.18:16: But Peter was standing at the door outside. Therefore the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
verses.18:17: Then the servant girl who kept the door said to Peter, "You are not also one of this man's disciples, are you?" He said, "I am not."
verses.18:18: Now the servants and the officers were standing by the burning coals, because it was cold, and were warming themselves; and Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.
verses.18:19: The high priest therefore questioned Jesus about His disciples and about His teaching.
verses.18:20: Jesus answered him, "I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews come together, and in secret I have spoken nothing.
verses.18:21: Why do you question Me? Question those who heard what I spoke to them; see, these people know what I said."
verses.18:22: Now when He had said these things, one of the officers standing nearby gave Jesus a slap, saying, "Do You answer the high priest like this?"
verses.18:23: Jesus answered him, "If I have spoken wrongly, bear witness about the wrong; but if well, why do you strike Me?"
verses.18:24: And Annas sent Him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
verses.18:25: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him, "You are not also one of His disciples, are you?" He denied it and said, "I am not."
verses.18:26: One of the servants of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter cut off, said to him, "Did I not see you in the garden with Him?"
verses.18:27: Peter therefore denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
verses.18:28: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. Now it was early morning, and they themselves did not enter the Praetorium, so that they would not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
verses.18:29: Pilate therefore went outside to them and said, "What accusation do you bring against this man?"
verses.18:30: They answered and said to him, "If this man were not a wrongdoer, we would not have handed Him over to you."
verses.18:31: So Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves, and judge Him according to your law." The Jews therefore said to him, "It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death."
verses.18:32: This was so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which He spoke, indicating by what death He was about to die.
verses.18:33: Pilate therefore entered the Praetorium again, and summoned Jesus, and said to Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?"
verses.18:34: Jesus answered, "Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you about Me?"
verses.18:35: Pilate answered, "I am not a Jew, am I? Your nation and the chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done?"
verses.18:36: Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world, My attendants would certainly be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jews; now, however, My kingdom is not from here."
verses.18:37: Pilate therefore said to Him, "So You are a king?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, that I may bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice."
verses.18:38: Pilate said to Him, "What is truth?" And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, "I find no grounds for a charge in Him.
verses.18:39: Now you have a custom that I should release one man for you at the Passover. Do you want me, therefore, to release for you the King of the Jews?"
verses.18:40: Therefore they all cried out again, saying, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a robber.
verses.19:1: So then Pilate took hold of Jesus and flogged Him.
verses.19:2: And the soldiers, weaving a crown from thorns, placed it on His head and wrapped Him in a purple robe.
verses.19:3: And they were coming to Him and saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" and they were slapping Him.
verses.19:4: Then Pilate went outside again and said to them, "Look, I am bringing Him outside to you, so that you may know that I find no grounds for a charge in Him."
verses.19:5: (So Jesus went outside, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment.) And he said to them, "Here is the man."
verses.19:6: So when the chief priests and the officers saw Him, they were shouting, saying, "Crucify, crucify Him!" Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves and crucify Him, for I myself find no grounds for a charge in Him."
verses.19:7: The Jews replied to him, "We have a law, and according to the law He must die, because He made Himself the Son of God."
verses.19:8: So when Pilate heard this statement, he feared all the more.
verses.19:9: And he entered the Praetorium again and said to Jesus, "Where are You from?" But Jesus did not give him a reply.
verses.19:10: So Pilate said to Him, "Do You not speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to crucify You, and I have authority to release You?"
verses.19:11: Jesus replied, "You would not have any authority against Me unless it had been given to you from above. For this reason, the one who handed Me over to you has a greater sin."
verses.19:12: And from then on Pilate was seeking to release Him. But the Jews were shouting, saying, "If you release this man, you are not a friend of Caesar. For everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar."
verses.19:13: Now when Pilate heard these statements, he brought Jesus outside and sat on the judgment seat, at the place that is called Lithostrotos, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
verses.19:14: Now it was the Preparation of the Passover, about the sixth hour, and he said to the Jews, "Here is your king."
verses.19:15: But they were shouting, "Take Him away, take Him away, crucify Him!" Pilate said to them, "Should I crucify your king?" The chief priests replied, "We have no king except Caesar."
verses.19:16: So then he handed Him over to them to be crucified. And they took Jesus and led Him out.
verses.19:17: And carrying the cross for Himself, He went out to what is called the Place of Calvary, and in Hebrew, Golgotha,
verses.19:18: where they crucified Him, and with Him two others, on this side and on that side, and Jesus in the middle.
verses.19:19: Now Pilate also wrote an inscription and placed it on the cross. And it was written: "Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews."
verses.19:20: Therefore many of the Jews read this inscription, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
verses.19:21: So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, "Do not write, 'King of the Jews,' but that He Himself said, 'I am King of the Jews.'"
verses.19:22: Pilate replied, "What I have written, I have written."
verses.19:23: Then when the soldiers had crucified Him, they took His garments (and made four parts, a part for each soldier) and the tunic. Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout.
verses.19:24: So they said to one another, "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots over it to decide whose it will be," so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, saying, "They divided My garments among themselves, and for My clothing they cast a lot." And indeed the soldiers did these things.
verses.19:25: Now standing beside the cross of Jesus were His mother, and His mother's sister, Mary of Cleopas, and Mary Magdalene.
verses.19:26: So when Jesus saw His mother, and the disciple whom He loved standing there, He said to His mother, "Woman, here is your son."
verses.19:27: Then He said to the disciple, "Here is your mother." And from that hour the disciple received her into his own household.
verses.19:28: Afterward, Jesus, knowing that all things had been completed, so that the Scripture might be completed, said, "I am thirsty."
verses.19:29: So a vessel full of vinegar was set there. And they, putting a sponge full of vinegar around hyssop, brought it to His mouth.
verses.19:30: So when Jesus had received the vinegar, He said, "It is completed." And bowing His head, He handed over His spirit.
verses.19:31: Then the Jews (since it was the Preparation), so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath day was a great one), asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away.
verses.19:32: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first one, and of the other who was crucified with Him.
verses.19:33: But after they came to Jesus, when they saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs,
verses.19:34: but one of the soldiers opened His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
verses.19:35: And the one who saw has given testimony, and his testimony is true. And he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
verses.19:36: For these things took place so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: "You will not break a bone of Him."
verses.19:37: And again another Scripture says, "They will look upon Him whom they pierced."
verses.19:38: Now after these things, Joseph from Arimathea (because he was a disciple of Jesus, though a secret one out of fear of the Jews) asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus. And Pilate gave permission. So he came and took away the body of Jesus.
verses.19:39: And Nicodemus also came, who had first come to Jesus at night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
verses.19:40: So they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with spices, as it is the custom for the Jews to bury.
verses.19:41: Now in the place where He was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.
verses.19:42: So there, because of the Preparation of the Jews, since the tomb was nearby, they laid Jesus.
verses.20:1: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came in the morning, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone removed from the tomb.
verses.20:2: Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, "They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have placed Him."
verses.20:3: So Peter went out, and that other disciple, and they came to the tomb.
verses.20:4: Now the two were running together, and that other disciple ran ahead faster than Peter, and came first to the tomb.
verses.20:5: And when he had bent down, he saw the linen cloths placed there; yet he did not go in.
verses.20:6: Therefore Simon Peter came following him, and went into the tomb, and saw the linen cloths placed there,
verses.20:7: and the facecloth that had been upon His head, not placed with the linen cloths, but rolled up separately in one place.
verses.20:8: So then that disciple who had come first to the tomb also went in, and he saw and believed.
verses.20:9: For they did not yet know the Scripture, that it was necessary for Him to rise from the dead.
verses.20:10: So the disciples went away again to their own place.
verses.20:11: But Mary was standing outside by the tomb, weeping. So while she was weeping, she bent down and looked into the tomb,
verses.20:12: and she saw two angels sitting in white, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been placed.
verses.20:13: They said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" She said to them, "Because they have taken my Lord, and I do not know where they have placed Him."
verses.20:14: When she had said these things, she turned back around and saw Jesus standing, and she did not know that it was Jesus.
verses.20:15: Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?" Supposing that He was the gardener, she said to Him, "Sir, if you have taken Him away, tell me where you have placed Him, and I will take Him away."
verses.20:16: Jesus said to her, "Mary." Turning around, she said to Him, "Rabboni" (which means "Teacher").
verses.20:17: Jesus said to her, "Do not touch Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father; but go to My brothers and say to them, 'I am ascending to My Father and your Father, My God and your God.'"
verses.20:18: Mary Magdalene came, announcing to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord, and He said these things to me."
verses.20:19: Therefore, when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled because of fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and said to them, "Peace be to you."
verses.20:20: And when He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side. Therefore the disciples rejoiced upon seeing the Lord.
verses.20:21: Therefore He said to them again, "Peace be to you. Just as the Father sent Me, I also send you."
verses.20:22: When He had said these things, He breathed upon them and said to them, "Receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.20:23: If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven them; and if you retain anyone's, they have been retained."
verses.20:24: However, Thomas, one of the Twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
verses.20:25: Therefore the other disciples said to him, "We have seen the Lord." He, however, said to them, "Unless I see in His hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into His side, I will not believe."
verses.20:26: And after eight days, His disciples were inside again, and Thomas with them. Jesus came with the doors shut, and stood in the midst and said, "Peace be to you."
verses.20:27: Then He said to Thomas, "Bring your finger here and see My hands, and bring your hand and put it into My side; and do not be unbelieving, but faithful."
verses.20:28: Thomas replied and said to Him, "My Lord and my God."
verses.20:29: Jesus said to him, "Because you have seen Me, Thomas, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and have believed."
verses.20:30: Indeed, Jesus also performed many other signs in the sight of His disciples, which are not written in this book.
verses.20:31: Now these things have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that, believing, you may have life in His name.
verses.21:1: Afterward Jesus manifested Himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. Now He manifested Himself in this manner:
verses.21:2: Simon Peter, and Thomas, who is called Didymus, and Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of His disciples were together.
verses.21:3: Simon Peter said to them, "I am going to fish." They said to him, "We are also coming with you." And they went out and boarded the boat, and that night they caught nothing.
verses.21:4: Now when morning had come, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
verses.21:5: Therefore Jesus said to them, "Children, you do not have anything to eat, do you?" They replied to Him, "No."
verses.21:6: He said to them, "Throw the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some." Therefore they threw it, and they were no longer able to pull it in because of the multitude of fish.
verses.21:7: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord." When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he fastened his tunic around himself (for he was naked) and threw himself into the sea.
verses.21:8: But the other disciples came in the boat (for they were not far from land, but about two hundred cubits), pulling the net of fish.
verses.21:9: So when they stepped down onto the land, they saw glowing coals placed there, and fish placed upon them, and bread.
verses.21:10: Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish that you have caught just now."
verses.21:11: Simon Peter went up and pulled the net onto the land, full of large fish, one hundred fifty-three; and even though there were so many, the net was not torn.
verses.21:12: Jesus said to them, "Come, have breakfast." And none of those dining dared to question Him, "Who are You?" knowing that it was the Lord.
verses.21:13: And Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and the fish in the same way.
verses.21:14: This was now the third time that Jesus was manifested to His disciples after He had risen from the dead.
verses.21:15: So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?" He said to Him, "Yes, Lord, You know that I love You." He said to him, "Feed My lambs."
verses.21:16: He said to him again, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me?" He said to Him, "Yes, Lord, You know that I love You." He said to him, "Feed My lambs."
verses.21:17: He said to him the third time, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me?" Peter was saddened because He said to him the third time, "Do you love Me?" and he said to Him, "Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You." He said to him, "Feed My sheep.
verses.21:18: Amen, amen, I tell you, when you were younger, you used to fasten your own belt and walk where you wished; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will fasten your belt and lead you where you do not wish to go."
verses.21:19: Now He said this, signifying by what death he would glorify God. And when He had said this, He said to him, "Follow Me."
verses.21:20: Turning around, Peter saw that disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who had also leaned back upon His chest at the supper and said, "Lord, who is the one who will betray You?"
verses.21:21: Therefore when Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, "Lord, but what about this man?"
verses.21:22: Jesus said to him, "So I want him to remain until I come; what is that to you? You follow Me."
verses.21:23: Therefore this word went out among the brothers that that disciple does not die. And Jesus did not say to him, "He does not die," but, "So I want him to remain until I come; what is that to you?"
verses.21:24: This is that disciple who bears testimony about these things and wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
verses.21:25: Now there are also many other things that Jesus did, and if these were written one by one, I think that not even the world itself could hold the books that would be written.

notes.1:2: Latin Hoc is neuter, agreeing grammatically with neuter Verbum ("the Word"), referring to the Word Himself.
notes.1:3: Latin punctuation attaches quod factum est ("that has been made") to verse 3 rather than verse 4.
notes.1:5: Latin comprehenderunt carries the dual sense of "grasped/understood" and "overtook/overcame."
notes.1:9: Latin reads in hunc mundum ("into this world") rather than simply "into the world."
notes.1:12: Latin filios literally reads "sons" rather than "children."
notes.1:13: Latin ex sanguinibus is literally plural ("from bloods"), rendered "from bloodlines."
notes.1:18: The Vulgate reads unigenitus Filius ("the only-begotten Son") rather than the Alexandrian Greek reading "only-begotten God."
notes.1:27: The Vulgate includes qui ante me factus est ("who has been placed ahead of me"), absent from the earliest Alexandrian Greek manuscripts.
notes.1:28: Latin in Bethania ("in Bethany") is followed here rather than the textual variant "Bethabara."
notes.1:29: The Vulgate doubles the exclamation: Ecce agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit ("Look, the Lamb of God; look, the One who takes away").
notes.1:42: The Vulgate reads filius Jona ("son of Jonah") rather than the Alexandrian Greek "son of John."
notes.1:51: Latin Amen, amen dico vobis keeps the Hebrew affirmation, rendered "Amen, amen, I tell you" consistently throughout the Latin Gospels; plural vobis ("to you") addresses those present.
notes.2:4: Latin "Quid mihi et tibi est, mulier?" renders a Semitic idiom, literally "What is it to Me and to you, woman?"
notes.2:6: Latin "metretas" refers to the Greek liquid measure metretes, roughly nine to ten gallons (about 39 liters) each.
notes.2:10: Latin "inebriati fuerint" literally means "have become drunk," though in biblical usage it can also convey drinking freely or to the full.
notes.2:17: The Vulgate reads the perfect/present "comedit" ("has consumed"), matching its rendering of Psalm 68:10 (69:9), whereas most modern Greek critical editions read the future "will consume."
notes.3:3: The Vulgate retains the Hebrew affirmation "Amen, amen" (meaning "truly, truly") and renders Greek "anothen" in its temporal sense as "denuo" ("anew/again"), paired with "renatus" ("reborn"), rather than "from above."
notes.3:5: The Vulgate explicitly reads "Spiritu Sancto" ("the Holy Spirit"), whereas most modern Greek editions read simply "Spirit."
notes.3:8: Latin "Spiritus ... spirat ... vocem" preserves a deliberate wordplay that can be read both as "the wind blows ... its sound" and as "the Spirit breathes ... His voice," echoing "born from the Spirit" at the end of the verse.
notes.3:11: The first-person plurals (scimus, loquimur, testamur, nostrum) are left lowercase because the text does not state whom Jesus includes with Himself.
notes.3:13: The Vulgate includes the closing clause "qui est in caelo" ("who is in heaven"), which is omitted in many modern Greek critical editions.
notes.3:31: No change of speaker is marked in the Latin text here; while John the Baptist's speech is kept open through 3:36, many interpreters end his direct speech at 3:30 and read 3:31-36 as the Evangelist's commentary.
notes.4:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'cognovit Jesus' ("Jesus came to know"), whereas many Greek manuscripts read "the Lord." In verse 2 the Vulgate also reads simply 'quamquam Jesus non baptizaret', without 'ipse' ("Himself").
notes.4:6: The Vulgate distinguishes 'fons' ("spring," used here and in 4:14 for living water) from 'puteus' ("well," used by the Samaritan woman in 4:11-12 for the deep dug shaft).
notes.4:10: The Vulgate translates the Greek contrary-to-fact particle with 'forsitan' ("perhaps"), yielding the distinctively Vulgate phrasing "you would perhaps have asked Him."
notes.4:11: Latin 'Domine' (vocative of 'Dominus') here and in 4:15, 4:19, and 4:49 is translated "Sir" as respectful address, though it is the same word used for "Lord."
notes.4:35: In the Clementine Vulgate, 'jam' ("already") belongs to the end of 4:35 ("already white for harvest") rather than the start of 4:36, which begins simply with 'Et' ("And").
notes.5:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads probatica piscina ("a sheep pool," treating probatica as an adjective modifying "pool" rather than "by the Sheep Gate") and names the pool Bethsaida rather than Bethesda or Bethzatha.
notes.5:18: In the Clementine Vulgate verse division, the clause introducing Jesus's discourse (Respondit itaque Jesus, et dixit eis) belongs to the end of verse 18 rather than the beginning of verse 19.
notes.5:28: The Vulgate distinctly reads vocem Filii Dei ("the voice of the Son of God"), echoing verse 25, whereas the Greek text reads "his voice."
notes.5:39: Latin Scrutamini (like the underlying Greek) is morphologically ambiguous and can be translated either as an indicative ("You search") or as an imperative ("Search").
notes.5:46: The Vulgate translates the Greek conditional particle with forsitan ("perhaps"), a distinctive Latin nuance preserved here.
notes.6:12: The Vulgate reads plural ne pereant ("so that they may not be lost"), referring directly back to fragmenta ("fragments"), whereas the Greek has singular me ti apoletai ("so that nothing may be lost").
notes.6:15: The Vulgate reads fugit ("fled"), aligning with Codex Sinaiticus and Old Latin witnesses, where most Greek manuscripts have anechoresen ("withdrew").
notes.6:17: The Vulgate uses the perfect venerunt ("came") rather than the Greek imperfect erchonto ("were going"), and omits "yet" in non venerat ("had not come", vs. Greek oupo).
notes.6:33: Because Latin panis ("bread") is masculine, the relative pronoun qui is grammatically ambiguous and may be read either impersonally ("that which") or personally ("He who" / "the One who"), anticipating Jesus's declaration in v. 35.
notes.6:41: The Vulgate explicitly reads panis vivus ("the living bread"), whereas the Greek text has simply ho artos ("the bread", reserving "living" for v. 51).
notes.6:51: Native Vulgate John 6 divides Saints.Bible 6:51 across native 6:51 ('I am the living bread...') and 6:52 ('If anyone eats from this bread...'), shifting native 6:53-72 one number higher than Saints.Bible 6:52-71.
notes.6:56: The Vulgate translates with the adverb vere ("truly", matching Byzantine/TR alethos), whereas critical Greek editions read the adjective alethes ("true food ... true drink").
notes.6:70: The Vulgate reads Christus Filius Dei ("the Christ, the Son of God"), differing both from critical Greek manuscripts ("the Holy One of God") and the Byzantine/TR addition ("of the living God").
notes.6:72: Because Iscariotem is accusative agreeing with Judam rather than genitive agreeing with Simonis, the Vulgate attaches the name Iscariot to Judas himself rather than to his father Simon.
notes.7:8: The Vulgate reads "I am not going up" (non ascendo), whereas many Greek manuscripts read "not yet" (oupo).
notes.7:22: The Vulgate places "Therefore" (propterea) at the start of verse 22 linked to Moses giving circumcision, whereas many modern editions attach the corresponding Greek phrase to the end of verse 21.
notes.7:32: The Vulgate reads "the rulers" (principes) here as in verses 26 and 48, distinct from "the chief priests" (pontifices) in verse 45 and the Greek archiereis ("chief priests").
notes.7:35: The Vulgate reads "of the Gentiles" and "the Gentiles" (gentium / gentes, also "nations"), whereas Greek manuscripts read "Greeks" (Hellenon / Hellenas).
notes.7:39: The Vulgate explicitly includes "given" (datus), whereas many early Greek witnesses read simply "for the Spirit was not yet."
notes.7:53: Unlike the Saints Greek Critical Text, the Vulgate includes 7:53-8:11 without double text-critical brackets.
notes.8:9: The Vulgate reads simply Audientes autem ("Then hearing this") without the expansion "convicted by their conscience."
notes.8:10: The Vulgate reads qui te accusabant ("those who were accusing you"), whereas shorter Greek manuscripts read simply "where are they?"
notes.8:11: Latin condemnabo is future tense ("Neither will I condemn you"), differing from Greek present-tense katakrino ("Neither do I condemn you").
notes.8:19: The Vulgate renders the Greek conditional particle with forsitan ("perhaps"), yielding the distinctively Vulgate phrasing "perhaps you would also know My Father."
notes.8:24: The Vulgate shifts from plural in peccatis vestris ("in your sins") to singular in peccato vestro ("in your sin"), where Greek texts use the plural in both clauses; quia ego sum is translated literally as "that I am" without supplying "He" (as also in 8:28).
notes.8:25: Principium can be nominative or accusative; it is rendered here as a noun ("The Beginning, who also speak to you"), as the first-person qui et loquor vobis suggests, whereas the corresponding Greek ten archen is usually taken adverbially.
notes.8:27: Vulgate quia Patrem ejus dicebat Deum ("that He was calling God His Father") reads ejus ("His") and explicitly includes Deum ("God"), whereas standard Greek texts read that He was speaking to them about the Father.
notes.8:45: The Vulgate reads conditional si ("if") rather than causal hoti ("because") found in Greek manuscripts.
notes.9:4: The Clementine Vulgate reads the singular "Me oportet" ("I must"), whereas many modern Greek critical editions read the plural ("We must").
notes.9:11: The Vulgate reads the present tense "et video" ("and I see") and includes "ad natatoria" ("to the pool of"), and similarly uses simple "videre" ("see") in 9:15 and 9:18 where the Greek uses "anablepo" ("receive sight").
notes.9:27: The Clementine Vulgate reads "et audistis" ("and you heard") without the negation found in the Greek ("and you did not listen").
notes.9:28: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive "sis" ("You be His disciple"), matching the imprecatory force of "Maledixerunt" ("cursed"), whereas the Greek uses the indicative ("You are his disciple").
notes.9:35: The Clementine Vulgate reads "Filium Dei" ("the Son of God"), whereas many modern Greek critical editions read "the Son of Man."
notes.10:8: The Clementine Vulgate reads "All, as many as came" (Omnes quotquot venerunt), omitting the phrase "before Me" found in many Greek manuscripts.
notes.10:11: The Clementine Vulgate reads "gives" (dat) and "his sheep" (ovibus suis), whereas the Greek uses the same verb "lays down" as in verses 15, 17, and 18 and reads "the sheep."
notes.10:16: The Clementine Vulgate reads "one fold" (unum ovile), repeating ovile from earlier in the verse, whereas the Greek distinguishes "fold" from "one flock."
notes.10:24: Literally "How long are You lifting up (or taking away) our soul?" (Quousque animam nostram tollis?), a literal Latin rendering of the Greek idiom for holding someone in suspense.
notes.10:29: The Clementine Vulgate uses the neuter singular "What My Father has given Me is greater than all" (quod ... majus), matching Codex Vaticanus rather than the masculine variant "My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all."
notes.11:27: The Clementine Vulgate distinctly reads "of the living God" (Dei vivi), "this world" (hunc mundum), and the second-person perfect "who have come" (venisti), where critical Greek texts read "of God, the one coming into the world."
notes.11:31: The Vulgate reads dicentes ("saying"), reflecting a Greek variant (legontes), whereas most modern critical Greek editions read doxantes ("supposing").
notes.11:33: Latin infremuit spiritu ("groaned in spirit," echoed by fremens in v. 38) conveys intense inner agitation, indignation, or audible groaning, and turbavit seipsum ("troubled Himself") is explicitly active and reflexive.
notes.11:35: Unlike the Greek text, the Vulgate begins with Et ("And"); its verb lacrimatus est ("shed tears") also distinguishes quiet weeping from plorare ("weep" aloud) in vv. 31 and 33.
notes.11:45: The Vulgate explicitly includes "and Martha" (et Martham) alongside Mary, whereas the Greek text names only Mary (compare also the Vulgate additions of "Mary" in v. 5, "born" in v. 37, and "And immediately" in v. 44).
notes.12:3: Latin pistici (borrowing Greek pistikos) is a rare term whose exact meaning is debated; it is usually understood as "genuine," "pure," or "unadulterated."
notes.12:19: The Clementine Vulgate reads first-person plural proficimus ("we are accomplishing nothing") and punctuates the clause as a question, whereas the Greek reads second-person plural ("you are gaining nothing").
notes.12:20: The Clementine Vulgate reads gentiles ("Gentiles"), whereas the Greek text reads Hellenes ("Greeks").
notes.12:25: The Clementine Vulgate places the conclusion of the grain-of-wheat saying ("it remains by itself alone...") at the start of verse 25 rather than verse 24, and pairs future perdet ("will lose") with present custodit ("keeps").
notes.12:32: The Clementine Vulgate reads neuter plural omnia ("all things"), reflecting an ancient textual tradition, where the majority Greek text reads masculine plural pantas ("all people").
notes.13:2: Latin coena facta literally means "supper having been made/done" (understood either as supper having been prepared/served or as supper having ended, contrasting with Greek critical texts' "during supper"). The Vulgate also reads in cor ("into the heart") without a possessive pronoun, with "Judas, son of Simon Iscariot" as subject of the betrayal clause.
notes.13:16: The Vulgate retains the loanword apostolus ("apostle"), literally meaning "one sent" or "messenger."
notes.13:18: The Vulgate reads the future tense levabit ("will lift up") and mecum panem ("bread with Me"), whereas many Greek manuscripts read a past tense ("has lifted up") and "My bread."
notes.13:31: Here and in 13:32 the Vulgate uses clarificare (an Ecclesiastical Latin synonym for glorificare, used in 14:13) for "glorify."
notes.14:1: Unlike the ambiguous Greek verb form, the Vulgate explicitly distinguishes indicative Creditis ("You believe") from imperative credite ("believe").
notes.14:2: Latin mansiones ("dwelling places") is cognate with manere ("remain") and mansionem ("a dwelling place") in 14:23. Following Clementine Vulgate punctuation, the second half reads as a statement ("if it were not so, I would have told you, because...") rather than a rhetorical question.
notes.14:10: The Clementine Vulgate reads the perfect tense fecit ("has done") with unadorned opera ("the works"), and uses plural creditis ("do you not believe") in both 14:10 and 14:11.
notes.14:11: The Clementine Vulgate repeats the question of 14:10a (Non creditis, "Do you not believe") rather than an imperative ("Believe Me"), and places alioquin propter opera ipsa credite ("Otherwise, believe because of the works themselves") at the beginning of 14:12.
notes.14:16: The Vulgate retains the Greek loanword Paraclitus ("Paraclete," meaning Advocate, Helper, or Comforter) here and in 14:26, unlike its use of advocatus in 1 John 2:1.
notes.15:2: Latin tollet ("will take away") and purgabit ("will prune" or "will cleanse") are future tense in the Vulgate, whereas the Greek uses present-tense verbs. Latin purgabit denotes both viticultural pruning and cleansing, connecting conceptually with mundi ("clean") in verse 3.
notes.15:6: The Vulgate uses future verbs (mittetur, arescet, colligent, mittent) with the singular pronoun eum ("him," or "it" referring to the branch, where the Greek has plural "them"), followed by an abrupt shift to the present tense ardet ("burns").
notes.15:15: Latin dicam ("I will... call") is future tense in the Vulgate, differing from the present indicative ("I call") in the Greek text.
notes.15:26: Latin Paraclitus retains the Greek loanword Parakletos, meaning "Advocate," "Counselor," or "Helper" (likewise in 16:7).
notes.16:5: The opening sentence ("Yet I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you") begins verse 5 in the Clementine Vulgate, whereas modern Greek editions place it at the end of verse 4.
notes.16:9: The Vulgate reads the perfect tense non crediderunt ("they have not believed"), contrasting with the present tense ("they do not believe") in the Greek text.
notes.16:13: The Vulgate reads docebit vos omnem veritatem ("He will teach you all truth"), a distinctive Latin rendering compared to the Greek "He will guide you into all the truth."
notes.16:16: The Vulgate includes the closing clause quia vado ad Patrem ("because I am going to the Father"), which is omitted in many modern critical Greek editions here though echoed by the disciples in verse 17.
notes.16:25: Latin proverbia (translating Greek paroimiai) refers here to veiled or figurative sayings rather than simple maxims; similarly in verse 29.
notes.17:1: The Vulgate renders the glory vocabulary throughout chapter 17 with clarifico and claritas (radiant splendor/glory), and includes tuus ("Your") in the second clause ("so that Your Son may glorify You"), where critical Greek editions read simply "the Son."
notes.17:11: The Clementine Vulgate reads masculine plural quos dedisti mihi ("those whom You have given Me"), referring to the disciples, whereas critical Greek editions read a neuter singular relative referring to the Father's "name, which You have given Me"; the same masculine plural begins the second sentence of 17:12 (Quos dedisti mihi, custodivi).
notes.17:15: Latin a malo is grammatically ambiguous and can be understood either as neuter ("from evil") or as masculine ("from the evil one").
notes.17:20: The Vulgate uses the future periphrastic qui credituri sunt ("who will believe"), whereas critical Greek editions have the present participle ("who believe").
notes.17:21: The Vulgate includes unum in the clause in nobis unum sint ("may be one in Us"), whereas critical Greek editions omit "one" there; likewise in 17:24, the Vulgate reads masculine plural quos ("those whom") rather than neuter singular ("that which").
notes.18:5: Latin Ego sum literally means "I am" without an expressed predicate "he" (likewise in 18:6 and 18:8).
notes.18:18: The Vulgate reads simply ad prunas ("by the burning coals"), omitting the Greek participial clause "having made a charcoal fire."
notes.18:30: The Vulgate uses the noun malefactor ("a wrongdoer" or "evildoer"), corresponding to the Byzantine/Textus Receptus reading rather than the critical Greek participial phrase "doing evil."
notes.18:38: Latin causam carries a legal sense ("ground for a charge," "case," or "fault"); in 18:40 the Vulgate also includes omnes ("all"), which is absent in critical Greek editions.
notes.19:10: The Clementine Vulgate places "to crucify You" before "to release You" (crucifigere te ... dimittere te), reversing the order in modern Greek critical editions; similarly, v. 20 orders the languages "Hebrew, Greek, and Latin."
notes.19:17: Latin Calvariae (the origin of English "Calvary") literally means "of a skull," corresponding to Greek Kraniou Topos; similarly, in v. 13 the Vulgate keeps the transliterated Greek place name Lithostrotos ("Stone Pavement").
notes.19:25: The Vulgate reads Cleophae, the same name it gives the disciple Cleopas in Luke 24:18, so it is rendered "Cleopas" here (the Greek text has Clopas). The genitive leaves the relationship implicit (traditionally "wife of Cleopas"), and the syntax permits counting either three or four women.
notes.19:34: The Clementine Vulgate distinctly reads aperuit ("opened") rather than the Greek verb for "pierced" or "stabbed," a wording noted by Latin patristic interpreters.
notes.19:36: The Vulgate renders the Scripture quotation with a second-person plural active verb (comminuetis, "you will not break"), echoing Exodus 12:46, whereas the Greek text uses a passive ("will not be broken").
notes.20:1: Latin literally reads "on one of the Sabbath" (una sabbati; similarly "una sabbatorum" in v. 19), a Semitic idiom for the first day of the week.
notes.20:10: Latin literally reads "to themselves" (ad semetipsos), an idiom for returning to their own lodging or quarters.
notes.20:17: Latin "Noli me tangere" literally means "Do not touch Me." The Clementine Vulgate also reads "to My Father" (ad Patrem meum) in the first clause, where the critical Greek text has "to the Father."
notes.20:18: The Clementine Vulgate places the second clause in the first person ("to me," mihi), whereas the Greek text uses the third person ("to her").
notes.20:25: Following an ancient variant, the Latin distinguishes "the mark of the nails" (fixuram clavorum) from "the place of the nails" (locum clavorum), where most Greek manuscripts repeat "mark" (typon).
notes.21:5: Latin "pulmentarium" refers to food or relish eaten with bread (often fish), rather than naming fish directly.
notes.21:12: The Clementine Vulgate reads "of those dining" (discumbentium, literally "of those reclining at meal"), whereas the Greek text reads "of the disciples."
notes.21:15: Here and in v. 16 Jesus uses "diligere" (devoted or esteeming love), while Peter replies with "amare" (warm, affectionate love); in v. 17 Jesus switches to "amare" as well.
notes.21:16: The Clementine Vulgate reads "Feed My lambs" (Pasce agnos meos) in both vv. 15 and 16 and uses "pasce" ("feed") in all three commands, whereas the Greek text reads "Shepherd My sheep" in v. 16.
notes.21:22: Here and in v. 23, the Clementine Vulgate reads "Sic" ("So" / "Thus"), expressing a statement ("So I want him to remain..."), whereas the Greek text reads "If" (ean).
